TITLE: CHECKOUT
LOGLINE: During a hurricane evacuation, a night concierge sees the same unknown woman on every security monitor — then every elevator opens onto black ocean water.
HOOK: The guest who never checked in is already inside the building. When the power dies, the hotel stops being on any map she knows.
SORA PROMPT — 12 SECONDS: Create a 12-second cinematic teaser for "CHECKOUT," a supernatural prestige thriller — hurricane luxury hotel, sodium emergency lighting, drowned-teal shadows, chrome rain on glass. Pacing: brutal 0.3–0.5s cuts tightening to 0.2s flash-frames at the drop. Needle-drop: low sub-bass pulse, distant generator thrum, one dead-silence beat before title.

[0:00–0:03 — Monitors]
Handheld whip through empty marble lobby, four security monitors flicker — the same pale woman in lobby, pool, corridor, rooftop at once. Hard cut: young concierge breath fogging the glass, reflection wrong by half a beat.

[0:03–0:07 — Evacuation]
Rapid-fire: guests in wet couture sprinting, PA distortion, palm fronds hammering windows. Flash-frames: room key, wristband, elevator indicator, ocean on a floor map that should read 12.

[0:07–0:11 — Flood]
Power snap. Every elevator door slides open to roaring black water instead of a floor. Concierge stares into the shaft — her face duplicated on a monitor behind her, smiling.

[0:11–0:12 — Title]
Vacuum silence. Whisper: "you're still checked in." CHECKOUT slams in chrome serif. Subsonic hit. Black.

Style: Anamorphic 2.39:1, halation on practicals, crushed blacks, magenta-cyan split-tone, Alexa grain. Faces lit from below. No logos. Blackout on final hit.

answer_text:
TITLE: THE LAST FLOOR
LOGLINE: A hurricane evacuation traps a night concierge in a coastal hotel where every camera shows a guest who does not exist — until the elevators open onto the ocean.
HOOK: She chases the stranger through four monitors and four impossible rooms. The final floor is not a floor at all.
SORA PROMPT — 12 SECONDS: Create a 12-second prestige horror sizzler for "THE LAST FLOOR" — luxury coastal hotel under evacuation, bruised storm light, wet marble, emergency amber strobing to morgue-blue. Pacing: 0.4s cuts, flash-frames on the impossible beat, one silence before title. Audio: hurricane muffled behind glass, elevator chime warping into whale-low sub-bass.

[0:00–0:03 — Signal]
Slow push on concierge desk phones ringing unanswered. Cut: quad-split security feed — identical woman in four locations, never moving her head.

[0:03–0:07 — Chase]
Sprint montage down service corridor, handheld, rain hammering skylight. Match cut through monitor glass into pool deck — empty except her footprint filling with water.

[0:07–0:11 — Drop]
All elevators ding at once. Doors open on churning black ocean at lobby level. Concierge's badge reflection shows a different name.

[0:11–0:12 — Title]
Hard silence. THE LAST FLOOR burns in white condensed type. Impact. Black.

Style: Restrained prestige horror, 2.39:1, practical halation, macro inserts on eyes and badges, no exposition cards.
